news.headline: KeyBanc reiterates Overweight on Forgent Power Solutions
news.summary: On the same day Morgan Stanley trimmed its target, KeyBanc stood by its Overweight rating, keeping it among the bulls on Forgent's data-center and grid-equipment demand. The average 12-month target has slipped to about $42, still roughly double the share price.

news.headline: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) Stock Price Target Cut by Morgan Stanley
news.summary: Morgan Stanley lowered its Forgent price target to $40 from $45 and kept an Equal Weight rating. The shares fell as much as 12% intraday on Friday to about $18.82, a new post-IPO low, after closing at $20.96 on Nov 19.

news.headline: Insider Buying: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) CAO Buys 3,000 Shares of Stock
news.summary: Chief Accounting Officer Inez Lund bought 3,000 shares on November 17, making her the fifth executive or director to buy on the open market since the post-Q1 selloff. The stock edged up to about $21.70 on November 18, even as Zacks Research cut its rating to Hold from Strong Buy.

news.headline: Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE:FPS) Stock Price Target Cut by Wells Fargo & Company
news.summary: Wells Fargo cut its Forgent price target to $25 from $44 and kept an Equal Weight rating, the most cautious of the post-Q1 target cuts. The note came the same day the shares gapped up on news of the cluster of insider purchases.

news.headline: Forgent CEO, CFO, a director and the general counsel buy shares after the post-earnings slide
news.summary: Form 4 filings dated November 16 show CEO Gary Niederpruem bought 16,000 shares at about $20.85-$21.59 (about $335K), CFO Amy Ard 14,617 shares at $20.52 (about $300K) and director Neel Bhatia 9,366 shares at $21.26 (about $199K); General Counsel Tyson Hottinger also reported buying 11,800 shares. It is the first cluster of open-market insider buying since the IPO, and the shares gapped up on November 17 after the filings.

news.headline: TD Cowen keeps Buy on Forgent, lowers price target to $55 from $76
news.summary: A day after fiscal Q1 results, TD Cowen kept its Buy rating but cut its target to $55 from $76, pointing to FY2027 bookings timing. Even after the cut, the target sits well above the low-$20s share price.

news.headline: Forgent shares slide despite Q1 beat as FY27 guidance midpoint trails estimates
news.summary: Despite record revenue of $478.6M (+69%) and adjusted EPS of $0.24 vs. $0.20 consensus, the stock fell as the raised fiscal 2027 revenue range of $2.45B-$2.65B had a midpoint below Street expectations. The stock was already down about 42% over the past month amid the data-center sell-off.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q2 2027 results
catalysts.detail: First quarterly check against the raised FY2027 guide of $2.45-2.65B revenue and $587-637M adjusted EBITDA; watch order intake and backlog conversion.

catalysts.label: Columbus office ramp
catalysts.detail: New 90,000 sq ft Columbus, Ohio office adding 85 jobs in support functions.

catalysts.label: Tijuana Powertrain expansion online
catalysts.detail: Expected to raise total revenue capacity to about $5.8B.

pulse: Forgent beat on Nov 12 with record fiscal Q1 revenue of $479M (+69%) and adjusted EBITDA of $105M, and raised its FY2027 guide to $2.45-2.65B revenue, with backlog already covering the full-year guide and hyperscaler orders building through 2028. The stock keeps sliding anyway because the guide midpoint trailed estimates: a wave of target cuts (Wells Fargo $25, JPMorgan $35, Morgan Stanley $40 on Nov 20, TD Cowen $55) and a Zacks cut to Hold pushed it down as much as 12% on Nov 20 to about $19, near its 52-week low. Insiders have answered with open-market buying (CEO, CFO, a director and the general counsel ~$1.08M on Nov 16, the CAO 3,000 shares on Nov 17); the next hard checkpoint is fiscal Q2 results around February.
